observations.name: One-record layout example
observations.analysis: One complete arity-one record is admitted by the shown incidence shape checks. One record yields one color with range [0,1], and ordered upload creates one populated u32 particle word. The distance shader text refers to particles[0] and particles[1] for constraint zero. The generic constructor stores supplied kernel and arity without a shown schema comparison; a conditional solve would need kernel acquisition, valid remaining bindings, native acceptance and actual dispatch. No shader or product code was run.

observations.name: Coloring counter capacity
observations.analysis: On a sufficiently provisioned 64-bit host, 2^32 distinct u32 particle indices can form 2^32 one-entry records with no shared address. The greedy algorithm can place all records in color zero; incrementing the u32 count for the final record exceeds u32::MAX at coloring line 135, before later ConstraintCount uniform/dispatch casts. Overflow behavior depends on compiler/profile policy; huge host allocations and earlier failure are not established. This is a source-level refinement of the historical native-capacity family, not an independent accepted count.

observations.name: Distinguished boundaries and safeguards
observations.analysis: The selected distance constructor derives arity-two records and checks rest-length cardinality; the selected Shell stretch/seam path uses that constructor and bending constructs arity four. Independently, attach_raw admits whole multiples of count without a selected-kernel record-width check, including an empty input; that is attachment width, not the incidence word width example. ParticleIndex assigns an ordinal role but not membership in the later particles buffer. These boundaries can share future ownership without being presumed aliases; normal Shell admission, supported callers and native access remain qualified.
